about: The viaducts ACT's 3D model lacks (it has buildings only; v1's bridges had piers but no arches). Modelled once, as data. Deck heights come from the transport graph (LiDAR surface model); everything else here is from the sources listed, and every number not in a source is marked as an assumption. Spec: v2/docs/specs/structures.md. Checked by check_structures.

pier_thickness_m.assumption: masonry piers of the 1860s Waring Brothers viaducts, typical 2.5-3.5 m along the deck; to verify on photos

deck_thickness_m.assumption: arch crown + spandrel to rail level over the crown (v1 used 1.6 m fascia)

arch_shape.assumption: the Luxembourg viaducts of 1859-1862 (Passerelle, Clausen, Pfaffenthal) use round arches

viaducts.name: Pulvermühl viaduct (Viaduc de Pulvermühl, Biisserbréck)

spans.source: en.wikipedia 'Pulvermuhl Viaduct': two abutments and four intermediate supports

viaducts.notes: Two parallel structures since 2019 (2 + 2 tracks): modelled as one deck over the OSM outline's width. OSM tags the outline bridge:structure=arch; fr.wikipedia describes hollow reinforced-concrete piers and a composite metal deck for the rebuilt structure. Arch vs beam is an open question for the owner (G0).

viaducts.name: Clausen viaduct (Viaduc de Clausen, Clausener Viaduc)

spans.source: fr/lb.wikipedia: largest span 15 m, length 208 m, height 44 m, 2 tracks
spans.assumption: all arches 15 m; count = round((length + pier) / (span + pier))

viaducts.name: Pfaffenthal viaduct (Viaduc de Pfaffenthal, Pafendaller Viaduc)

spans.source: fr.wikipedia: 257 m (lb: about 260 m, 32 m high), masonry arch bridge by the same builders as Clausen
spans.assumption: arches like the Clausen viaduct's (15 m); count = round((length + pier) / (span + pier))

viaducts.notes: Continues the Clausen viaduct directly (a bridge over the Montée de Clausen joins them). OSM maps only part of its deck as rail bridge ways; the deck line here is the OSM outline's long axis where the rail ways do not cover it.
